title: Muharram: a fresh year
hook: a new Hijri year and a renewed intention
tomorrow: one day holds two memories, a rescue and a grief. how?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a new month: it begins when someone looks up and sees it. Once a year, that thin crescent opens more than a month.

New Year's Eve: a countdown, confetti, a list of resolutions that might last a week. The Islamic year starts with one more thin crescent, the one that opens Muharram, and no fireworks at all. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahl ibn Sa'd says the companions didn't count their years from the call of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, or from his death, but from his arrival in Medina: the hijra, the move. So the year begins at a moving day. How should it be marked?
screen: `A COUNTDOWN, CONFETTI.` → `ONE MORE CRESCENT.` → `COUNTED FROM THE MOVE.`

segments.voice: Muslims answer two ways, and each has a case. One view says: mark it. Greet each other, take stock, set a fresh intention. The case: the very first report in Sahih al-Bukhari says actions are judged by intentions, and it's told through the hijra itself: whoever migrated for God and His Messenger, that is what the migration was for. A year counted from a migration is a natural moment to ask what you're moving toward. And the month matters in its own right. Another report names Muharram among the four sacred months, and in Sahih Muslim, fasting in God's month, al-Muharram, is called the best fast after Ramadan. The other view says: keep it plain. No report shows the Prophet or his companions marking the turn of the year, and acts of worship are best kept as they were taught. The case: added rites can crowd out what was actually given. So fast in Muharram, which is taught, and let the date pass quietly. Now notice how much the two share. Neither throws a party. Both point to the same month, the same fast, the same intention renewed. Where they part is whether the first night deserves a greeting. Either way, a fresh year is a direction, not a countdown.
screen: `MARK IT: A FRESH INTENTION.` · `A SACRED MONTH, A TAUGHT FAST.` · `KEEP IT PLAIN: NO NEW RITES.` · `SAME MONTH, SAME FAST.` · then, large: `A FRESH YEAR.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and write one intention for the year ahead, in a single line, by hand. Not a list: one direction, the way a migration has a direction. Toward what? Fold the paper and keep it where you'll find it next Muharram.
screen: `ONE LINE, BY HAND.` · `ONE DIRECTION.` · `FOLD IT. KEEP IT.`

segments.voice: Muharram: the first month of the Islamic year, one of the four sacred months, opening a year counted from the hijra.
Here's the thought: a fresh year is a direction, not a countdown. Day three of this part, behind you.

howItsDone: At the start of Muharram some Muslims exchange new-year greetings and set intentions, while others keep the day plain; some fast voluntarily during the month, especially around its tenth day.

fork.setup: your cousin says greeting the hijri new year is fine and harmless. you lean that way too. state the plain view's best case.
options: no report shows it marked; keep worship as taught, and fast instead.
greetings are rude to people who don't use the hijri calendar.
the calendar came later, so Muharram itself doesn't really count.
fork.reveal: the plain view rests on there being no report of the turn of the year being marked, and on keeping worship as it was taught. it still honors Muharram's fast.

chat.meaning: One view marks the year with greetings and a renewed intention; the other keeps it plain, with no new rites. Both honor Muharram's fast.

hijra.meaning: the Prophet's migration from Mecca to Medina
